Circular tracks

Source: R/geom-track.R
geom_track.Rd

A track is an ordinary ggplot2 layer whose angle comes from the plot's layout and whose radius is scaled into a declared radial band. Node ids are translated to angles when the layer is added; the scale factors live in a position_track() position, so the same normalisation is reused by every track and can be applied by hand to your own geoms.

Usage

geom_track(
  mapping = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  ...,
  geom = "col",
  node = NULL,
  value = NULL,
  band,
  stack = FALSE,
  scales = c("free", "fixed"),
  limits = NULL,
  baseline = NULL,
  width = 0.9,
  offset = 0,
  position = NULL,
  slot = NULL,
  domain = NULL,
  origin = 0,
  na.rm = FALSE,
  show.legend = NA,
  inherit.aes = FALSE
)

Arguments

mapping, data, show.legend, inherit.aes, na.rm, ...

Standard ggplot2::layer() arguments.

geom

Which track geometry to use: "col"/"bar" (anchored at the band's inner edge), "area", "boxplot", "violin", "density", "point", "tile" or "text". The last three sit at the band's centre when no x is mapped; with an x they land at the scaled value, the way a bar's outer edge does. "violin" and "density" both put a node's density along its arc, with the value along the radius: "violin" fills the outline, "density" draws it as an open curve, so several distributions can share a band without covering each other. Both take n, adjust and trim, passed to stats::density() (see ...).

node

Unquoted name of the column holding node ids. Required.

value

Unquoted name of the column holding the values to plot, e.g. value = gc. Optional (aes(x = gc) also works), but it is the robust spelling: value is handed to the position directly, so it keeps working when the data has a column literally called x and it makes stack able to reject negative input instead of silently drawing a flat track.

band

Either a declared track name (see the tracks argument of ggcircos()) or an explicit c(r0, r1) radius interval.

stack

Stack values within each node instead of scaling them independently. Values must then be non-negative. Not available for the aggregating geoms ("boxplot", "violin", "density"), whose stat has already folded each node into one mark.

scales

"free" normalises each node against its own range; "fixed" uses limits for every node.

limits

Value range of the track; required when scales = "fixed".

baseline

Lower bound when scales = "free". By default 0 if all values are non-negative, else the smallest value.

width

Fraction of a node's arc covered by the layer.

offset

Distance from the band's inner edge. Only meaningful when band is an explicit interval.

position

A position_track() object. NULL (the default) builds one from this layer's band/stack/scales/limits/node arguments; pass an existing one to reuse the same normalisation across layers (see the escape hatch under position_track()). When given, those settings come from the position, not from this call.

slot

Optional: a column of the track data holding the link row number (edge_id) each row belongs to. Given it, the row occupies the arc that its link's slot occupies – a track drawn per link sits exactly on the link's foot, the way circlize's per-link annotation rectangles do (spec §4.10). Without it, a node's rows split its arc evenly.

domain

Optional: a node-table column holding each node's coordinate ceiling – the top of its axis, the way a chromosome length runs 0 .. length. Only used by interval tracks (aes(xmin = start, xmax = end)), where it decides the scale a node's start-to-end range is normalised against, per node. Without it each node is scaled to the largest xmax its own rows report.

This is the maximum, not the span: giving max(xmax) - min(xmin) puts intervals past the top of their own axis, and that is rejected rather than drawn flat.

origin

Lower bound of the interval coordinates, 0 by default. Give 1 for a 1-based coordinate system.

Value

A ggplot2 layer.

Normalisation

With band [r0, r1] and per-node scale "free", a value v maps to r0 + (r1 - r0) * (v - base) / (max - base), where base is baseline. With "fixed", base and max are limits. With stack = TRUE, values are converted to within-node fractions first. "boxplot" maps its xmin/xmax quantiles through the same affine map; anchored geoms stretch from r0 to the mapped value. "violin" and "density" map the values they sampled the density at, so the distribution is turned sideways inside the band: broad where the samples pile up, narrow where they thin out.

Examples

set.seed(1)
vals <- data.frame(
    id = rep(colnames(mtcars), each = 4),
    value = runif(ncol(mtcars) * 4),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ggcircos(cor(mtcars), order = "hclust", tracks = c(values = 0.2)) +
    geom_chord(aes(fill = r)) +
    geom_track(data = vals, aes(x = value), node = id, geom = "col", band = "values")


# a violin: several samples per node, the density spread along the arc
set.seed(2)
samples <- data.frame(
    id = rep(colnames(mtcars), each = 40),
    value = rnorm(ncol(mtcars) * 40, 0.5, 0.1),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
ggcircos(cor(mtcars), order = "hclust", tracks = c(dist = 0.3)) +
    geom_node_arc() +
    geom_track(data = samples, aes(x = value), node = id,
               geom = "violin", band = "dist")


# the same density as an open curve, for comparing several nodes in one band
ggcircos(cor(mtcars), order = "hclust", tracks = c(dist = 0.3)) +
    geom_node_arc() +
    geom_track(data = samples, aes(x = value), node = id,
               geom = "density", band = "dist", colour = "steelblue")
